L8-PDF1-p1.text:
108 Finger Permutations - Level 8
Two-Position Ladder: 4+4 Whole-Pattern Shift Control
Level 8 begins the horizontal-mobility branch. String-crossing difficulty is intentionally removed so the hand can learn one new task: release, relocate, and rebuild the four-fret frame without losing
time.
1. Keep two fret frames fixed
P5: 1=5, 2=6, 3=7, 4=8.
P7: 1=7, 2=8, 3=9, 4=10.
Use the assigned finger in both frames.
Do not stretch from P5 to fake the move.
2. Echo the complete code
Play all four digits in P5.
Shift the hand two frets as one unit.
Repeat the same four digits in P7.
Return by reversing the two frames.
3. Make the shift inaudible
Release pressure before moving.
Keep fingertips close to the strings.
Move the thumb with the hand frame.
No scrape, slide, pause, or extra accent.
Worked example - code 1234
The barline is the shift boundary. The aligned one-string template is repeated on each string in the printed route; the notes are not played as a
chord.
SHIFT UP - E > A > D > G > B > e
P5                         P7
S|5-6-7-8----|7-8-9-10---|
SHIFT DOWN - e > B > G > D > A > E
P7                         P5
S|7-8-9-10---|5-6-7-8----|
PASS 1
Play as even eighth notes. Insert one deliberate subdivision at the barline, release pressure, move the whole frame, and lightly
accent the first note after the shift.
PASS 2
Remove the pause and accent. Keep both four-note cells identical in volume, articulation, and tempo. Then convert the phrase to
straight sixteenths.
The frame must move even when overlapping fret ranges make a stretch seem possible.
Practice protocol
1
Choose one 12-exercise set.
2
Begin 10-15 BPM below your clean Level 1 same-string
tempo.
3
Play SHIFT UP and SHIFT DOWN with a downstroke start.
4
Repeat both routes with an upstroke start.
5
After three clean loops, add 2 BPM at the next session.
6
After two late landings, squeaks, or tension, reduce 4-6
BPM; require two clean days.
Standard tuning. P5 = frets 5-8; P7 = frets 7-10. Repeat the one-string template on each string in route order.

L8-TXT1-1-25.text:
108 FINGER PERMUTATIONS - LEVEL 8: TWO-POSITION LADDER
4+4 whole-pattern position-shift control in standard tuning.
P5 mapping: 1=index/fret 5, 2=middle/fret 6, 3=ring/fret 7, 4=pinky/fret 8.
P7 mapping: 1=index/fret 7, 2=middle/fret 8, 3=ring/fret 9, 4=pinky/fret 10.

MOVEMENT RULE
Play the complete four-digit code in fifth position, release pressure, shift the entire hand frame two frets,
and repeat the same code in seventh position. For the return route, play the code in seventh position first,
then shift down and repeat it in fifth position. The shift occurs only between complete four-note cells.
Play SHIFT UP on E-A-D-G-B-e and SHIFT DOWN on e-B-G-D-A-E, one string at a time.
The repeated aligned tab lines are a compact map; they are not simultaneous chord tones.

WHY THIS IS LEVEL 8
Levels 1-7 developed vertical movement while the fretting hand remained in fifth position. Level 8 starts the
horizontal-mobility branch. It deliberately removes in-cell string crossing so release pressure, target-fret
accuracy, thumb movement, and hand-frame reconstruction can be learned as separate skills.

PRACTICE RULE
Use one 12-exercise set per session. Begin 10-15 BPM below your clean Level 1 same-string tempo.
First pass: play even eighth notes, pause one subdivision at the center barline, and lightly accent the first
note after the shift. Second pass: remove the pause and accent, then convert the 4+4 phrase to straight 16ths.
Play both routes with a downstroke start, then repeat with an upstroke start. Because each cell contains four
notes, the second cell begins with the same pick direction; this keeps the new difficulty in the fretting hand.
After three clean loops, add 2 BPM next session. After two late landings, fret squeaks, errors, or rising tension,
reduce 4-6 BPM. Advance after the full set is clean in both directions on two separate days.
